invariant: ADR-0055 §1 (as amended 2026-11-06, #30905, ruling record 6687830530) — `resolveCbpRelation` derives a `controlled_by_parent` object's master from exactly one `master_detail` field declared `required: true` that names a reference, or, with none, from the object's ONLY `master_detail`, declared `required: false` and naming a reference: an OPTIONAL master (`CbpRelation.optional`), picked by the spec's own `controlledByParentMasterOf` so the parse and this reader cannot name different fields. A detail row that names its master is read through it, and a required master's read leaf is byte-identical to before; a row whose master reference is empty is read through the null-master arm of `computeControlledByParentFilter` alone, by the row's owner (`owner_id`, only where the detail carries that column) and by View All on the detail; the write gate still refuses a write that leaves the reference empty. Anything else resolves `null`, which both halves treat as fail-closed (reads answer RLS_DENY_FILTER, writes throw MasterDetailRelationMissingError, 422 INVALID_METADATA), reported once per object per cache generation: no `master_detail`, two or more required ones, two or more with none required, and one whose `required` is not written at all (this reader tests `required === false`, never its absence, so an object that reached the registry without the parse resolves no master). Do NOT restore the retired fallback tiers (any `master_detail`, then a required `lookup`) or a first-by-field-order pick among two: they were never part of ADR-0055 §1, `ObjectSchema` refuses those shapes at parse, and a gate that derives access from a relation the parse refuses is the disagreement the step-18 semantic migration `cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired` closed. Do NOT widen the null-master arm past rows whose master reference is empty, or let View All on the detail open the master arm. The reference-SPELLING tolerance in the same reader is a different, deliberate decision and stays.
